background_definition.rule: 1996 household income at or below its weighted percentile cutoff; ties kept together
background_definition.reference_population: Selected panel, birth years 1980-1984 pooled, each respondent counted once

literature_motivation.citation: Chetty, Raj, David J. Deming, and John N. Friedman (2026). Diversifying Society's Leaders? The Determinants and Causal Effects of Admission to Highly Selective Private Colleges. Quarterly Journal of Economics 141(1): 51-145.
literature_motivation.location: Section 6.1, p. 43, and Table V, row 7, in the August 2025 author version
literature_motivation.use_in_source: The need-affirmative admissions counterfactual gives the bottom parental-income quintile the largest boost, following Chetty et al. (2020). This is not the source paper's earnings-regression specification.
literature_motivation.source_income_measure: Parental household income averaged over child ages 12-17, ranked against parents of children in the same national birth cohort; negative parental income is excluded.
literature_motivation.adaptation: Single-year 1996 household income in the selected NLSY97 panel, pooling birth years 1980-1984 with custom person weights. Genuine negative baseline income is retained. These are sample-relative ranks, not national birth-cohort ranks.
literature_motivation.foundational_reference: Chetty, Friedman, Saez, Turner, and Yagan (2020). Income Segregation and Intergenerational Mobility Across Colleges in the United States. Quarterly Journal of Economics 135(3): 1567-1633. https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjaa005

education_definition.source: Highest degree earned by the 2015 interview
education_definition.pooled_groups: Codes 0/1 pool no degree and GED; codes 5/6/7 pool master's, doctoral, and professional degrees.

formula: wage_2025 ~ education_category(reference=high_school) * low_background + asvab_percentile + female + age + race + factor(year)
estimation: Weighted pooled OLS; same respondent sampling weight in every earnings year
covariance: Respondent-clustered sandwich with weighted scores and CR1 factor G/(G-1)*(N-1)/(N-K)
inference: Two-sided Student-t tests and 95% pointwise confidence intervals with G-1 degrees of freedom; categorical model additionally reports the joint CR1 Wald F(4,G-1) test of interactions

sample.weighting: custom sampling weights normalized to mean 1

limitations: Associations, not a causal difference-in-differences design.
Screening-confirmed zero wage amounts are included; unresolved skips and other missing amounts remain excluded.
The definition and reference population of family background are inherited from stage 2; see background_definition and its source/adaptation notes.
Inference conditions on the chosen background definition and does not adjust for estimated-cutoff uncertainty, multiple pointwise contrasts, or the full survey design.

Education is degree status at the 2015 interview, not college attendance or updated degree status; the high-school reference can include people who attended college without earning a postsecondary degree.
Earlier exploratory specifications were examined before this revision; this is not a preregistered analysis.
